title: [News] SK hynix Reportedly Joins Samsung in Licensing YMTC’s Xtacking Technology as NAND Race Heats Up
html:
China’s memory makers are challenging global rivals not just through aggressive capacity expansion, but increasingly on the technology front. According to Nikkei, Samsung and SK hynix have struck cross-licensing deals with YMTC, gaining access to elements of its proprietary Xtacking technology as they advance their 3D NAND architectures.

Samsung is already moving toward commercial adoption. As The Herald Business reported, it secured access to YMTC’s hybrid bonding patents last year. Kim Jae-jun, executive vice president of Samsung’s memory business, revealed during its second-quarter earnings call that volume production of its 10th-generation V-NAND, combining bonding with triple-stack technology, was slated to begin in August, according to the report. Nikkei’s latest report suggests that YMTC’s patent reach now extends to both Korean memory giants.

Why Xtacking Matters in the 400-Layer NAND Race

Nikkei explains that first introduced in 2018, Xtacking involves fabricating memory cells and their controlling CMOS circuitry on separate wafers before bonding them together to form a 3D NAND chip, with the method allowing memory cells and CMOS circuitry to be fabricated and optimized independently. YMTC, as noted by the report, says it began volume production of Xtacking-based 3D NAND in 2019.

As a 2025 ZDNet report explained, through the 300-layer class, South Korean chipmakers have adopted an architecture in which memory cells are stacked above the peripheral circuitry that controls them on a single wafer: As Samsung calls this approach Cell-on-Periphery (COP), SK hynix refers to it as Periphery Under Cell (PUC).

However, as NAND layer counts reach 400 or more, mounting stress on the underlying peripheral circuitry can cause damage, the ZDNet report noted, adding that Korean memory makers have therefore opted for wafer-to-wafer (W2W) hybrid bonding, which involves fabricating memory cells and peripheral circuits on separate wafers before bonding them together.

The shift toward hybrid bonding is gaining urgency as Korean memory giants push the limits of NAND stacking. According to The Herald Business, Samsung unveiled its 400-plus-layer, 10th-generation V10 BV (Bonding Vertical) NAND at FMS 2026, while SK hynix showcased its 375-layer, 10th-generation 4D NAND. YMTC, by contrast, demonstrated roughly 294-layer NAND at FMS 2025.

YMTC’s Growing Technology Moat

Citing industry sources, SR Times suggests YMTC published 119 hybrid bonding-related patents between 2017 and January 2024. By comparison, Samsung Electronics reportedly held 83 such patents and SK hynix just 11 as of 2023.

Beyond sheer patent numbers, a separate analysis by BLT Patent & Law Firm reveals distinct technological strongholds: SanDisk holds industry benchmark patents, TSMC commands critical IP in stacking-induced stress and wafer warpage control, while YMTC has built an extensive patent network around vertical interconnect structures.

Against this backdrop, Nikkei suggests that Korean chipmakers will struggle to circumvent YMTC’s existing patents when adopting wafer bonding, making licensing necessary to facilitate technology development and prevent potential patent disputes.
